standard_prerequisites: the perfect generator of D_QCoh(O_X) for X proper, flat and of finite presentation over a ring (theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh of the same chapter)
the identity lim O_X tensor M_n = Rlim O_X tensor M_n for systems with surjective transitions (lemma-Rlim-quasi-coherent of the same chapter)
RHom_X(E, -) is exact and commutes with products, hence with derived limits (Cohomology on Sites, global RHom section)

the duality formula RHom_X(E, O_X tensor M) = RGamma(X, E^vee tensor^L Lf^*M) = RGamma(X, E^vee) tensor^L M for E perfect (sites-cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex and lemma-cohomology-base-change of the same chapter)
RGamma(X, E^vee) is a perfect complex of R-modules for E perfect and f proper, flat, of finite presentation (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general of the same chapter)
pseudo-coherent complexes commute with tensoring and filtered limits (More on Algebra, Lemma more-algebra-lemma-pseudo-coherent-tensor-limit)
core_obligations: Prove that for f : X -> Spec(R) proper, flat and of finite presentation and any inverse system (M_n) of R-modules with surjective transition maps, the canonical map O_X tensor_R (lim M_n) -> lim O_X tensor_R M_n induces an isomorphism from the source to DQ_X applied to the target, i.e. it induces isomorphisms Hom(E, source) -> Hom(E, target) for every E in D_QCoh(O_X)
proof_roadmap: D_QCoh(O_X) has a perfect generator, so it suffices to verify the isomorphism of Hom sets for perfect E.

The limit is a derived limit (lemma-Rlim-quasi-coherent), and RHom_X(E, -) commutes with products and derived limits, so Hom(E, lim O_X tensor M_n) = Rlim RGamma(X, E^vee) tensor^L M_n after the base change identification.

RGamma(X, E^vee) is perfect, hence pseudo-coherent, and pseudo-coherent complexes commute with derived limits of modules, giving Rlim RGamma tensor M_n = RGamma tensor lim M_n, which is the required isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: H3: a generator-reduction argument combined with duality and a pseudo-coherent limit commutation, each step quoted from a standard lemma.
